description: HEM-1 golden: a machine-guard / enclosure SIDE PANEL — a 300 x 180 mm blank at 1.5 mm gauge with a 20 mm CLOSED HEM folded back on BOTH long edges (the safe-edge treatment a real guard panel gets on its two exposed sides). Deliberately NOT a small fixture: 6x the linear size of closed-hem-plate, a DIFFERENT gauge (1.5 mm, so the gauge-PROPORTIONAL hem radius rule is exercised rather than assumed to scale), and TWO hems rather than one. Both take the DEFAULT radius — neither carries bend_radius_mm — because the defect this golden exists to catch is a DEFAULT-behaviour defect: a hem labelled 'closed' that inherits the part's general bend radius builds an open hem. On this panel the old rule would have opened a 5.00 mm gap (2 x the part's 2.5 mm base-flange radius) between two layers that are supposed to be pressed together.
tangent_line_convention: Flat length is measured to the bend TANGENT LINES (§9 #1). The base flange's developed leg is the full length of its flat top face (300 mm, tangent line to tangent line); each hem return's developed leg is its own flat face length (20 mm). Each bend allowance BA REPLACES the two setback segments a sharp-corner unfold would use. A hem is a 180-deg fold, so each developed strip is the SAME kind of BA strip any bend produces; both bend-table rows read angle 180 deg.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill). Dims: base flange 300 x 180 mm (developed leg 300, width 180), TWO hem returns of developed leg 20 mm on the two edges at x = 0 and x = 300, gauge t = 1.5 mm, fold angle 180 deg = pi, K = 0.44 (v1 default). The base flange's own default bend radius is 2.5 mm and is deliberately left set: no hem may reach for it.

HEM RADIUS (HEM-1): neither hem sets bend_radius_mm, so each radius comes from the hem TYPE and the GAUGE — r = HEM_CLOSED_RADIUS_RATIO * t = 0.05 * 1.5 = 0.075 mm. Because the rule is a ratio of GAUGE, this 1.5 mm panel gets a different radius from the 2 mm closed-hem-plate; that is the point of goldening a second gauge.

AIR GAP (the property the hem's NAME asserts): gap = 2*r = 0.15 mm = 0.1 x gauge, on BOTH hems. Measured on the built solid as the distance from each hem's parent flat (its recorded base_face_signature plane) to the nearest face that faces back at it: 0.15000000000000124 mm on both, residual 1.22e-15 vs analytic. Under the pre-HEM-1 rule this would have been 5.0 mm (2 x the part's 2.5 mm base-flange radius) — 3.3 gauges of air inside a 'closed' hem.
Bend allowance (§1): BA = angle_rad * (r + K*t) = pi * (0.075 + 0.44*1.5) = pi * 0.735 = 2.3090706003884982 mm per hem.
Flat length (§9 #1): flat_length = base_leg + 2*(BA + hem_leg) = 300 + 2*(2.3090706003884982 + 20) = 344.61814120077702 mm. Measured == analytic (residual 0.0).

Developed area (§9 #2, neutral-surface conservation): flat_area = flat_length * width = 344.61814120077702 * 180 = 62031.26541613986 mm^2 (the blank is a rectangle: both hems fold off opposite full-width edges, so nothing notches the outline).
Fold direction is inferred from the geometry (§5): both hem returns fold to the +normal side of the base flange, so direction = 'up' for both. Fold angle = 180 deg exactly.

Fused body volume = base plate (300*180*1.5 = 81000) + two hem returns (per-hem cross-section 20*1.5 + half-annulus (pi/2)((r+t)^2 - r^2) = (pi/2)((1.575)^2 - (0.075)^2) = (pi/2)*2.475; cross-section = 30 + 3.8877209127605915 = 33.887720912760592, x 2 hems = 67.775441825521183, * 180 width = 12199.579528593813) = 93199.579527174254 mm^3 (analytic). Each return sits 2*r = 0.15 mm above the base — 1500x the kernel's 1e-4 mm linear tolerance — so the layers are near-contact but NOT coincident, and find_zero_width_slits reports nothing.

content_hash is the sha256 of the provenance-driven FlatPattern.to_json_bytes(). It is a DETERMINISM PIN (byte-identity), not analytic -- reproducible in-process AND across a fresh interpreter restart (§9 #4).
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill). Measured deviations vs the hand-derived values (2026-08-28, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9): flat_length residual 0.0, flat_area residual 7.28e-12 (the 180 mm width multiplies the arc-fit noise), bend_width residual 0.0, worst BA residual 1.2e-14, worst resolved inner-radius residual 3.83e-15. Documented ceiling 1e-9 leaves ~2 orders of headroom over the largest observed residual while staying tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m). The volume tolerance (1e-6) covers the measured 1.46e-11 residual on a 93 199 mm^3 body with 4 orders to spare.
air_gap_rationale: Measured first, then set. The gap is a difference of two parallel plane offsets on axis-aligned geometry; the measured residual vs the analytic 2*r is 1.22e-15 mm on both hems. The 1e-12 ceiling is ~3 orders above that worst observed residual and 8 orders BELOW the kernel's 1e-4 mm linear tolerance, so it can neither drift into a false failure nor admit a gap the kernel would consider a different place. Same ceiling as closed-hem-plate at a different gauge, which is the cross-check that the measurement is a property of the fold and not of one model.
